questions.q: Why is adding a new optional field to a schema considered non-breaking?
options: A consumer reading specific fields by name and type is unaffected by a new field it never asked for
Adding fields is never actually possible in a data contract
It's only non-breaking if the consumer explicitly approves it in advance
All schema changes are breaking by definition, with no exceptions
questions.explain: Anything that changes what a consumer is already relying on is breaking, regardless of how small it looks.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a breaking change be made by editing Lesson 50's contract in place?
options: A new version should exist alongside the old one, both emitted during a transition period, rather than silently substituting one for the other
Contracts can never be changed once published, under any circumstances
Editing in place is actually the correct approach and versioning is unnecessary
Only Databricks tables support versioned schemas, not Fabric contracts
questions.explain: Change is normal, but it has to be announced and staged, not silently substituted.

options: A transition period where both the old and new forms of a field are emitted, giving consumers time to migrate at their own pace
A fixed, universal number of days required before any schema change
A window that only applies to KQL Databases, not other Fabric items
The time it takes CI/CD to deploy a change to production
questions.explain: Its length is a judgment call depending on how many consumers exist and how quickly they can realistically move.

questions.q: How does this lesson's versioning and deprecation window relate to Lesson 39's real-time schema drift detection?
options: Lesson 39 catches an unannounced change as it happens; this lesson's approach is how a producer changes the schema deliberately, without becoming that kind of surprise
They are unrelated topics with no connection
Schema drift detection replaces the need for contracts and versioning entirely
Deprecation windows are only relevant to batch pipelines, not real-time ones
questions.explain: The contract and its versioning process is exactly what's meant to prevent the failure mode Lesson 39's detection exists to catch.

questions.q: Which of these is a breaking change, according to this lesson?
options: Renaming FareAmount to TotalFare
Adding a new optional field like TipAmount
Adding a new value to an existing enum
None of these are breaking changes
questions.explain: Renaming a field changes what an existing consumer is already relying on, unlike purely additive changes.
